alignments.note: Presentative frame; the *that* goes to the apodosis waw under rule 45.
Present preposition takes the *of* of *inquired of*.
Fronted auxiliary to the interrogative particle (rule 17).
Quantifying construct numeral takes *any*; the *of* is the rectum's (rule 19).
*anointed David king* leaves the ל nothing (rule 40).
Separately written name components take their distinct ASV words under rule 2; the opening component retains the construct relation's of (rule 19).

Written relative takes the supplied antecedent *they that* (rule 46 rider); the copula joins it because the predicate is the nominalized relative clause and its finite verb cannot bear a second clause (rule 20). Competing reading: *were* on the subject noun as sole free anchor.
Construction-supplied copula joins the participial predicate (rule 20).
*even unto* is the preposition's whole expansion; no waw stands beside it (rule 16).
*requite you* promotes the object; the preposition keeps nothing (rule 40).
*Now therefore*: the adverb takes *Now*, the waw the *therefore* (rule 14).
Jussive frame *let ... be strong* belongs to the verb (rule 17).
Resultative ל left nothing by *be ye valiant* (rule 21).
*sons of strength* → *valiant* fused (rule 30); headed on ḥayil, which carries the lexeme; competing head the construct s009.
Rectum takes the *of*; discontinuous around the possessive.

*which [was] to Saul* → *Saul's*: one English word carries the relative, the possessive ל and the name (rules 30, 49); headed on the name which the word writes. Competing reading: ʾăšer unrepresented beside a ל+name fusion.
Hiphil *brought ... over*; particle completes the lexeme (rule 44).
Supplied *to* for the directional accusative belongs to the noun (rule 33).

review_notes: ASV margin (Eshbaal) read and set aside.

alignments.note: Appositional suffix (*Israel, all of it*) rendered by nothing; *all Israel* writes no pronoun.
Age בֶּן takes *old* with the copula (rule 58).
*began to reign* is the ASV's rendering of the ingressive infinitive.
*were after* → *followed*: one word carries copula and preposition (rule 30); headed on ʾaḥărēy, which carries the content. Competing head the verb s020.
The main verb *was* of the whole clause.
*number of the days* → *time*: one word writes neither lexeme exactly, so the construct heads as syntactic head (rule 23); competing head yāmiym.
Article takes the phrase's *the* (rule 30's chronicles pattern).
*from this [side]* recast as *side of*; the relation goes to מן. Competing reading: מן unrepresented with *of* inside the demonstrative's unit.
Deictic *this* rendered as contrastive *one side*, supplied determiner and generic noun joining (rules 15, 31).
Jussive frame *Let ... arise* discontinuous around subject and particle.
*young men* for נַעַר; the ASV never writes bare *men* for it, so *young* carries the lexeme (rule 31). Competing head *men*.
Compound numeral rendered by one word.
Supplied lexical verb (italic) for a verbless clause (rule 20).
Margin gloss read and set aside.
עַד־מְאֹד → *very* fused (rule 30), headed on the adverb carrying the content.
Supplied *the* goes to the counted noun, not the numeral (rule 15).
Comparative *as ... as* is one rendering of the כְּ, discontinuous, headed on the relational second *as* (rule 24's degree-word reasoning).
*one of the roes* → *a roe*: the numeral is rendered by the indefinite article.

*which [are] in the field* → *wild*: the relative supplies the attributive relation, ב the field-location, and שדה the lexical content, jointly expressed in one adjective under rule 30 and headed on the noun. The article's determination is not expressed: *wild* describes a class rather than naming a definite time or place, so rule 30's definite-adverb exception does not apply. The margin corroborates the underlying clause without replacing the printed target.
The separately segmented article has no determiner or determination expressed in lexical *wild*; it is unrepresented under rules 12, 29 and 30.
Gerund recasting writes *in* for the ל (rule 52).
Fronted copula to the interrogative particle (rule 20).
Predicate wholly elided: copula joins the sole subject pronoun (rule 20). Competing reading: *It is I* whole on the pronoun.
Light verb *lay hold* heads on the complement; the *on* is the valency preposition reaching the bare object (rule 44).
As 2.14: *young* carries the lexeme; competing head *men*.

יָסַף + עוֹד rendered by the single *again*, which carries both the verb's repetition and the adverb's; fused under rule 30 rather than leaving עוֹד unrepresented beside a rendered verb, as 2SA.2.28 fuses יָסְפוּ עוֹד → *any more*. Headed on the finite verb as syntactic head; competing readings: *again* on the verb alone with עוֹד unrepresented (rule 56), or on עוֹד with the verb unrepresented.
No *to* written; the infinitive is the English finite verb (rule 52).
לָמָּה → *wherefore* fused; headed on the interrogative carrying the content, competing head the preposition as syntactic head.
*lift up* → *hold up*; particle completes the lexeme.

review_notes: Corrected s002/s003: one *again* stands for the pleonastic pair יָסַף עוֹד, so the two fuse under rule 30 instead of leaving עוֹד unrepresented.

alignments.note: *hinder end* for אַחֲרֵי (the back part); supplied *the* on the construct; head on *hinder* (rule 31).
מֵאַחֲרֵי → *behind* fused (rule 30); headed on the content-bearing אַחַר.
תַּחַת with suffix rendered *in the same place*; the preposition's own lexeme is what *place* writes here.
The suffix's referent (*his*) realized as *same* (rule 18's lexical realization). Competing reading: suffix unrepresented with *same* inside the preposition's unit.
Frame keeps its *that*: the apodosis opens with a fronted subject (casus pendens) and the waw on the verb is resumptive, not apodosis-opening, so rule 45's waw case does not arise; contrast 2.1.

Kol takes the quantitative expression as many, headed on many. The competing fusion with the article is unnecessary because the following as independently realizes the article's relative function (rules 2 and 41).
The substantival article takes the second as, which introduces the relative restriction on as many (rule 41).
The participle retains came; the written article separately carries the relative realization.
Relative with resumptive *there* rendered by one *where* (rule 22).
Resumptive waw before the apodosis verb; the ASV writes no connective for it (rule 14).

review_notes: Variant WLC.2SA.2.23.v001 (s028–s029) is underdetermined and resolved to r00-base; the English *in the same place* is compatible with it and no fallback exclusion applies.

Reconciliation: fused s032+s033 (כָּל־הַ) → *as many as*, headed on כֹּל and *many*, since the second *as* is the article's relative sense and rule 30 forbids leaving a morpheme unrepresented whose sense the rendering carries (cf. 1CH.26.28 *whosoever*).

variant_decisions.evidence: Qere תַּחְתָּיו and ketiv תחתו are spelling variants of the same form ("in his place"); ASV 'died in the same place' renders either identically, with no italic supply or textual note distinguishing them. Base qere fallback retained.

alignments.note: *went down* for the sun's setting; particle completes the lexeme.

עַל־פְּנֵי → *before*; *lieth* is the locative copula the ASV writes where *is* would stand and joins the prepositional predicate (rules 20, 49). Competing reading: *lieth* added as a supplied lexical verb.
Adverbial accusative takes the supplied *by* and *the* (rules 33, 29).
Hithpael reflexive and the *together* completing *gather* stay with the verb (rule 44).
*one hill* → *a hill*: the numeral is rendered by the indefinite article, as in 2.18.
Matrix duration frame *how long shall it be* (rule 17); first source token as display anchor (rule 6).
Oath formula *As ... liveth* belongs to the adjective (rule 55).
לוּלֵא carries both the condition and the negation, discontinuous around the verb.
מן rendered *in*; margin (Hebrew *from the morning*) read and set aside.
Niphal *gone up (away)*; particle completes the lexeme.
No conjunction or negative stands in the Hebrew for *nor* (rule 14).
*from after* recast as the verb *followed*; one word carries both morphemes (rule 30).
יָסַף + עוֹד rendered together as *any more* (rules 30, 56); the finite verb keeps the subject pronoun *they*. Competing reading: עוֹד alone on *any more* with the verb unrepresented.
The infinitive is the English finite verb; no *to* written (rule 52).
Intransitive הָלַךְ keeps the bare *went*; the *through* is the accusative of extent's own (rule 33), as *to Mahanaim* is in this verse.

כָּל־הַבִּתְרוֹן is an adverbial accusative of place traversed, not a direct object of הָלַךְ, so the supplied *through* goes to the nominal it stands before under rule 33, which is the construct quantifier opening the phrase. Competing readings: *through* on the verb as a valency preposition (rule 44), or on the name as the noun carrying the case-function.

review_notes: Corrected the *through* of *went through all Bithron*: the phrase is an adverbial accusative of place under an intransitive verb, so rule 33 places the supplied preposition on the nominal rather than rule 44 on the verb, consistent with *to Mahanaim* in the same verse.

alignments.note: Apodosis waw with no connective written (rule 14).
Presentative dummy joins the finite verb (rule 17).
Supplied result subordinator (italic) over an asyndetic clause (rule 55).
*took up* for נָשָׂא; particle completes the lexeme.
Bare place name as locative predicate: supplied *in* belongs to the noun (rule 33) and the copula joins the predicate (rule 20).

Impersonal *it grew light* rendered *the day brake*; the supplied subject writes the verb's own daybreak lexeme and joins its unit (rule 44's lexeme test). Competing reading: *the day* added under rule 17.
